title: Due west from London
hook: London looks level with New York across the ocean. Is it?

knows: London is in Europe and New York is across the Atlantic
a world map has level lines of latitude
doesNotKnow: which landmass London's latitude lines up with
that the big US east-coast cities line up with Spain and Portugal

misconception: London shares a latitude with New York or Washington, since both are across the Atlantic.
objective: The learner can say that London's latitude meets Canada across the Atlantic, while Madrid's and Lisbon's meet the United States and New York's meets Portugal.

claims.text: London is at 51.5°N, Madrid 40.4°N, New York 40.7°N and Lisbon 38.7°N.
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: gazetteer values London 51.5072 N 0.1276 W, Madrid 40.4168 N 3.7038 W, New York 40.7128 N 74.0060 W, Lisbon 38.7223 N 9.1393 W. The stage uses exactly these.

claims.text: Going west along London's latitude, the first country met across the Atlantic is Canada (at about 55.5°W).
claims.source: Builder's node walk (0.1 degree steps, d3-geoContains over the kit's Natural Earth 1:110m countries, first country after open sea): London -> Canada at 55.5 W; an earlier 0.05 degree walk gave 55.48 W after 3,737 km. The stage computes the same walk in the browser. Coarse data: see c6.

claims.text: Going west along Madrid's latitude (and Lisbon's), the first country met across the Atlantic is the United States.
claims.source: Same walk: Madrid -> United States at 74.0 W; Lisbon -> United States at 75.1 W.

claims.text: Going east along New York's latitude, the first country met across the Atlantic is Portugal.
claims.source: Same walk: New York eastward -> Portugal at 8.7 W (then Spain).

claims.text: On an equirectangular map, lines of latitude are level (horizontal) lines.
claims.source: Snyder (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual: in the equirectangular projection x is proportional to longitude and y to latitude. From memory, not re-checked.

claims.text: On the coarse stage map the line from London clears Britain and then meets open sea; real Ireland touches that latitude, so the stage skips it.
claims.source: The 1:110m data has no polygon at 51.5 N between 4.2 W and 55.5 W (builder's walk). That Ireland's southwest coast reaches about 51.5 N is from the builder's memory of the map (Cork/Kerry coast near 51.5 to 52 N); needs a checker.

claims.text: Europe sits much further north than it feels.
claims.source: Follows from c1-c4: London (51.5 N) is 10.8 degrees of latitude north of New York (40.7 N), about 1,200 km (10.8 x 111.2 km). Opinion word 'feels' is a framing, not a measurement.

claims.text: Hook: London looks level with New York across the ocean.
claims.source: Framing of the common impression that the two cities face each other; a statement about how a viewer may read a map, not a measured fact. Needs a source or softer wording.

recall.question: Which two cities share about the same latitude: London and New York, or New York and Madrid?
recall.why: New York (40.7 N) and Madrid (40.4 N) are nearly level; London is at 51.5 N, in line with Canada.
